hints: Look at the $y$ against $x$ graph and read off the amplitude in $\text{mm}$ and the length of one full cycle in $\text{cm}$ from $x = 0$ to $x = 4.0\text{ cm}$.
Use the wave equation $v = f\lambda = \lambda / T$ with $v = 20.0\text{ cm s}^{-1}$ to convert that wavelength into the oscillation period $T$ in $\text{s}$.
Check which $y$ against $t$ graph has the same $\pm 1.0\text{ mm}$ swing about zero, starts at $y = 0$ rising, and completes one cycle in your calculated $T$.
walkthrough: Read amplitude and wavelength from the $y-x$ graph. The peaks reach $\pm 1.0\text{ mm}$, so amplitude $A = 1.0\text{ mm}$. The pattern repeats from $x = 0$ to $x = 4.0\text{ cm}$, so wavelength $\lambda = 4.0\text{ cm}$.
State the governing relation for a progressive wave: $v = f\lambda$ and $T = 1/f$, so $T = \lambda / v$.

Substitute values with units: $T = 4.0\text{ cm} / 20.0\text{ cm s}^{-1} = 0.20\text{ s}$. The particle must therefore oscillate about $y = 0$ with amplitude $1.0\text{ mm}$ and period $0.20\text{ s}$.
At the left end of the $y-x$ plot the displacement is $y = 0$ and rising toward $+1.0\text{ mm}$, so the $y-t$ curve must also start at $0$ and rise first.
Only the graph with $\pm 1.0\text{ mm}$ vertical scale, zero crossing at $0.10\text{ s}$ and full cycle in $0.20\text{ s}$ starting upward satisfies all three checks. This is option A.

A.explanation: Amplitude $1.0\text{ mm}$ and period $0.20\text{ s}$ match the wave, starting at $y=0$ moving positive.

B.explanation: Amplitude is correct but period $4.0\text{ s}$ is 20 times too large for $\lambda = 4.0\text{ cm}$ and $v = 20.0\text{ cm s}^{-1}$.

C.explanation: Shows $y$ from $0$ to $+2.0\text{ mm}$ only and period $4.0\text{ s}$, so both amplitude range and time scale are wrong.

D.explanation: Shows $y$ from $0$ to $+2.0\text{ mm}$ only and period $5.0\text{ s}$, so it does not oscillate about zero with the correct period.
